hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: paraplane execution rules apply to any plan with a ```paraplane block and take precedence over this skill's instructions: dispatch every task of a wave in parallel (one message, one subagent per task, each limited to its owns, its prompt carrying a line Paraplane-Task: <plan path> <task id>); subagents never commit; after the wave run `paraplane audit <plan> <wave>`, then the wave's gate, and fix until both pass; then the coordinator commits the wave with trailers Paraplane-Plan: <plan path> and Paraplane-Wave: <wave id> in the last paragraph of the message, with Co-Authored-By and other trailers and no blank line between them. Only when the project's own rules require another scheme: one commit per stage (audit with every wave of the stage so far, `paraplane audit <plan> W1,W2`, and list them all in that commit, one Paraplane-Wave trailer each), or one commit per task (the coordinator commits each task after its review, one at a time, with trailers Paraplane-Plan: <plan path> and Paraplane-Task: <task id>; the audit and the gate still run after the wave, which needs no commit of its own). Progress: a hook records a task when its subagent ends, before the task's review, and shows the progress to the user by itself, so do not repeat it. A Paraplane-Task line is recorded only as a line of its own whose plan path has no spaces and is a plan file of plan_paths, whose id is a task of that plan, and among the first 16 such lines of the prompt; it counts toward the progress shown only while the plan has no E errors. When a recorded task fails its review, undo the record with `paraplane progress --forget <ids> <plan>`. Full rules: skill paraplane:rules.
